player: the sample player (invented for pass charge-to-world-1; no real person)

q1.words: a small recording studio in the garage, to make music with friends

gets: evenings with friends that have a point

already.free: humming in the car on the way home

q3.risk: quiet evenings alone that ask nothing of anyone

keys.sadness: The music I care about is one evening away, not a lifetime.

q6.hoard: the half-finished songs, kept in the toolbag so nobody hears them

drafted.strong_start: Every branch the player brushes hangs lower, and the toolbag on their back drags at the shoulders. Rain ticks on the leaves. Ahead, through the trees, a hum of music starts, and stops mid-bar.
secrets: The half-finished songs are lighter than the toolbag.
The friends already have a key to the garage.
The Weigher's scale reads the bag, never the song.
The stump in the clearing answers any note, even a wrong one.
The hum that stops mid-bar is the player's own, from a year ago.
Oriel kept a recording of the last time they played together.
The broken bridge needs one plank, and the toolbag already holds it.
The Tinker built the Scale-House and regrets it.
The rain stops in any place where a song is played to its end.
The Protector carries the bag because it once kept the songs safe from laughter.

encounter.name: The Unfinished Clearing
aspects: a ring of instruments grown into the tree trunks
a bar of music that loops and stops
a stump that sounds a note when you do

villain.name: The Scale-House
aspects: a hut built of stacked brass weights beside a broken footbridge
air thick and amber, smelling of oil
a brass balance in the doorway whose pan holds your toolbag

road-home.name: The Friends' Fire
aspects: a low fire ringed with upturned crates for seats
laughter and a guitar being tuned
an empty crate left for you

npc_lines.Oriel: Play what you have so far?
npc_lines.the Tinker: Weights only weigh what you put in the pan.
npc_lines.the Protector: If nobody hears it, nobody can say it's bad.

capability.act: Play one unfinished song for one person this week.
